findings.evidence: crossing_isolated_right requires only ht₀ ∈ Ico (min a b) (max a b) (line 108–110) and crossing_isolated_left ht₀ ∈ Ioc (min a b) (max a b) (line 124–126); both include the endpoints. RegularityConditions.lean:235 states finite_crossings : ∀ s ∈ S, (Icc a b ∩ γ⁻¹'{s}).Finite with no endpoint-avoidance, and the basepoint field (line 242) explicitly handles γ a ∈ S — so the ha/hb form cannot discharge that field when the basepoint is a prescribed singularity, the case it exists for.
findings.fix: Drop ha, hb. Replace the ht₀_Ioo step with a case split on t₀ = min a b / t₀ = max a b / interior, discharging the endpoint cases via the existing crossing_isolated_right / crossing_isolated_left.
findings.issue: finite_crossings assumes ha : γ a ≠ z₀ and hb : γ b ≠ z₀, but the theorem holds without them. An infinite crossing set accumulates at some t₀ ∈ [[a,b]]; if t₀ is an endpoint the accumulation is one-sided, and crossing_isolated_right (t₀ ∈ Ico min max) / crossing_isolated_left (t₀ ∈ Ioc min max) — both already proved here and covering the endpoints — already forbid it. ha/hb are used only to force t₀ into Ioo so the two-sided eventually_ne_nhdsNE applies.

summary: The endpoint hypotheses ha, hb on finite_crossings are stronger than necessary: the isolation lemmas already in the PR cover the endpoints from the interior side, and the stated downstream field ConditionAprime.finite_crossings carries no such assumption.
